messages:
deploy-bot: Rolling out release 2.5.1 -> canary (12% traffic) in us-west-2. change-window: 23:00-03:00 UTC. canary-id=canary-1956. Monitors: p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-quality-regressions. auto-rollback: enabled with default thresholds.
maya: quick question — what are the auto thresholds currently set to?
alice: deploy-bot status message included: auto-rollback triggers = (p95 >= baseline*1.35 for 5m) OR (5xx >= 0.7% for 5m) OR (slo_errors >= 5 for 3m).
ben: those 5xx limits look tight for model busy windows — recommend we add a manual gate at 25% canary and hold for 10m before continuing.
release_mgr: agreed with Ben. We'll do staged advance: 12% -> hold 10m -> 25% -> hold 10m -> 50% -> full. Manual approval required at 25%.
oncall-bot: @channel Pager duty: @tim is oncall for infra. Alerts will fire to #eng-oncall if 5xx spike.
tim: oncall ack — I'll keep an eye on p95 dashboards. If we see sustained regressions I'll initiate fallback.
maya: adding runbook notes here for if we need to rollback quickly. Please keep responses short so ops can act.
maya: Runbook (short):
1) If auto-rollback triggers, deploy-bot will start canary abort and shift traffic back to 2.4.9. Confirm in channel.
2) If manual rollback: oncall runs: `deploybot rollback --target 2.4.9 --canary canary-1956 --reason "p95-regression"`
3) Pin fallback in registry: `redwoodctl pin model-server --version 2.4.9 --scope global`
4) Notify CS + sales with templated blurb.
5) Create incident and tag #postmortems if customer-impacting.
alice: small note — if caching/KV mismatch suspected, prefer graceful split rollback instead of full pin; use `deploybot split-traffic --from 2.5.1 --to 2.4.9 --percent 80` to reduce blast radius.
ben: agree. Also check KV-cache version header in request logs: `x-kv-version`. If mismatch, do split then flush caches.
release_mgr: comms: if rollback happens, CS sends this to impacted customers: "We observed regression after today's deploy and have reverted to previous version. No action needed on your side; we're investigating." @cs_lead can you prep fuller note?
cs_lead: on it. I'll draft a short FAQ and push to #customer-comms once we decide rollback.
oncall-bot: Alert rule: Canary fail count >=3 in 5m -> post to this thread and page oncall.
tim: If I get paged I'll run the rollback command and then post the command output here. Keep me posted on product/regressions.
maya: decision tree quick:
- Non-customer-affecting perf blip (single AZ): wait 10m, check retries + infra metrics.
- p95 up >35% or sustained 5xx >0.7% across AZs: trigger rollback.
- Model-quality (generation) regression flagged by eval harness: hold and escalate to model-oncall, may pin older model if accuracy severe.
ben: Also, if automated rollback fires, ops should still confirm CS comms before closing the incident.
release_mgr: Action items now:
- @tim watch for pages (oncall)
- @alice and @ben watch canary dashboards for 25% gate
- @cs_lead prepare customer note draft
- @maya I'll be ready to approve manual rollbacks if needed

alice: advancing to 25% now (manual step).

deploy-bot: Canary advanced to 25% traffic. canary-id=canary-1956. next hold: 10m.

maya: good. small reminder to ops: if you run the rollback command please copy/paste output here (no screenshots).

timecheck: 10m hold started.

(last msg) maya: thread will be updated with any abort/rollback actions. If we end up rolling back we'll attach the incident number and postmortem link.
